title: Life Sciences Operator, External Research
description: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the role Anthropic's Life Sciences team is building a world-class research group focused on making fundamental biological discoveries. The team combines cutting-edge AI with hands-on biological research, positioning Anthropic at the forefront of AI-accelerated scientific discovery. This role offers a unique opportunity to shape how AI transforms biological research. We are looking for an experienced leader to take responsibility for how our research gets executed, across every program and field we work in. AI is making it much faster to generate scientific ideas, and testing them is now the harder problem. As our Life Sciences Operator for research, you'll be a key partner to our research teams, who work across many fields of biology. You'll build the relationships, the team, and the systems that turn their ideas into results quickly and to a high scientific standard. You'll help build our approach to operationalizing science. The ideal candidate is self-directed and has built a career in organizations that hold a high bar for scientific and operational rigor. Key responsibilities Turn research ideas into well-scoped experimental plans with clear milestones and criteria for success Select and manage the external partners best placed to run each project, and coordinate work that spans more than one Build a team of internal and external experts with the breadth the science requires Manage a large portfolio of concurrent projects and see each one through with speed and ownership Keep research leadership informed on progress, turnaround time, and outcomes Orchestrate research agendas with Claude and our internal agent frameworks Build insights into where AI-driven research planning works and where it falls short, and share them with the model-improvement and product teams as evaluations, datasets, and failure cases Minimum qualifications Experience at a contract research organization (CRO), biotech, or pharmaceutical company, accountable for delivering experimental programs for other scientists from scoping to final data Established record of scoping, placing, and managing outsourced experimental work with several CROs at once, from either the sponsor side or the CRO side Ability to take an idea from outside your own field, find the right expert, and judge whether a plan is executable and sensibly scoped Experience running many projects in parallel, and the ability to show how you tracked, prioritized, and reported on them Use of AI tools as a default part of how you work, and interest in finding out how far that can go Comfort navigating ambiguity and developing solutions in rapidly evolving research environments Results orientation, with a bias towards flexibility and impact Preferred qualifications A PhD in a biological science, bioengineering, or a related field Existing working relationships with CROs across several experimental areas, and a network you can call on to find new ones Experience as a study director or project lead at a CRO, or leading external research at a biotech or pharmaceutical company Hands-on breadth across more than one experimental area Experience scaling an operational function through a period of rapid growth The annual compensation range for this role is listed below. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. Annual Salary: $320,000 — $405,000 USD Logistics Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices. Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this. For roles performing work in California: We will consider for employment all qualified applicants, including those with arrest or conviction records or criminal histories, in a manner consistent with the requirements of applicable state and local laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the City of Los Angeles’ Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act. We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team. Your safety matters to us.
